filename: Parametrization in Weather and Climate Models _ Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Climate Science.pdf
title: Parametrization in Weather and Climate Models
venue: Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Climate Science
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review article synthesizing parametrization concepts, traditional physical closures, stochastic formulations, and machine learning approaches across atmospheric and oceanic models. No new dataset is created or distributed.
pain_points: Lack of clear scale separation / the gray zone where unresolved and resolved fluxes are of comparable magnitude
Compartmentalization of processes leading to compensating biases between parameterization schemes
Online numerical instability of ML parameterizations despite high offline training accuracy
Difficulty enforcing conservation laws (mass, momentum, energy) in ML and stochastic parameterizations
Generalization/universality to unseen climate regimes and across different model resolutions or configurations
Data scarcity and computational cost of generating high-resolution simulations needed for training
extraction_notes: Encyclopedia review paper providing conceptual framing of subgrid parameterization, Reynolds decomposition, stochastic schemes, and machine learning methods in atmospheric and oceanic models.
